compatibility_baseline.reason: The exact pre-assumption rollback still exited 11 online. The cited ee6db437 benchmark allocates compact group_sum rows, while the tutorial text says padded rows. This baseline supports both layouts from host-visible tensor shapes and reverts kernel scheduling to the cited compiler-compatible two-stage organization.
compatibility_baseline.address_selection: storage_rows == routed_weight_rows selects compact raw_start+token_offset; otherwise padded block_start
compatibility_baseline.route_dtype_selection: supports FP16 and FP32 route-weight tensors
compatibility_baseline.offset_lengths: specializes independently for E or E+1 tensors
compatibility_baseline.formal_sota_retained: H17F2 remains the compact research SOTA but is not claimed as online-deployed performance

online_incident.reported_symptom: OJCHAL v1 followed by native Python traceback-handler segfault and exit code 11
online_incident.corrected_causal_assessment: Removing T.assume did not fix the online crash, so assumptions are not established as the root cause. Layout mismatch or old online lowerer incompatibility remains the leading explanation.
online_incident.re_enable_optimized_schedule_only_with: successful evidence from the exact online evaluator

synchronized_mechanisms.formal: H17F2 remains the measured compact research baseline
synchronized_mechanisms.submission_adaptation: conservative original-style two-stage schedule selected because exact-online native failures invalidate deployment of the optimized schedule

synchronized_mechanisms.formal: compact group metadata translates padded block coordinates through raw group offsets
synchronized_mechanisms.submission_adaptation: runtime specialization supports compact raw_start+token_offset and tutorial padded block_start address spaces
compact route indexing is retained with controlled FP16 or FP32 route tensor annotation

promotion_policy: A formal SOTA and ten-argument submission must be integrated together. When the exact online contract or lowerer is ambiguous or native-crashes, deploy a hash-bound conservative compatibility baseline, validate every plausible ABI locally on real C500, and do not claim formal benchmark speedup as online performance.
